q: 1. A point determined by resection on a plane table is called
explain: When the position of the plane table station is determined by resection from known points, the resulting located point is termed a 'plane table fix'.

q: 2. While surveying a plot of land by Plane tabling, the field observations
options: and plotting do not proceed simultaneously
and recorded in field books to be plotted later
explain: The key characteristic of plane table surveying is that field observation and plotting are done together at the same time in the field, unlike other methods where plotting is done later in the office.

q: 3. Plotting of inaccessible points on a plane table, is done by
explain: Inaccessible points (points that cannot be reached to measure distance) are plotted by the method of intersection, sighting the point from two known plane table stations and drawing rays to fix its position.

q: 4. The technique of plotting all the accessible stations with a single set up of plane table is called
explain: Radiation is the method in which rays are drawn from a single plane table station to each visible (accessible) point, and distances are plotted to scale along these rays, all from one setup.

q: 5. Radiation plane table survey is the best suited when
explain: Radiation requires measuring the actual distance from the instrument station to each point, so it is best suited when the points are both close by and physically accessible for chaining.

q: 6. Locating the position of plane table station with reference to three known points, is known as
explain: When the plane table station's position is determined with reference to three known points visible on the ground, this is specifically termed the three-point problem (a case of resection).

q: 7. The 'fix' of a plane table from three known points, is good, if
options: either the right or left station is nearest
explain: As per the book's answer key, the quality of the 'fix' from three-point resection depends on the geometric configuration (strength of fix relative to the great circle), not simply on which station is nearest, so none of these applies directly.

q: 8. The size of plane table is
explain: A standard plane table board used in surveying is typically 750 mm x 900 mm in size.

q: 9. In plane tabling, the instrument used to measure horizontal and vertical distances directly, is known as
explain: As noted earlier, a telescopic alidade, fitted with stadia hairs, allows both horizontal and vertical distances to be measured directly in plane table surveying.

q: 10. The plotting of small areas which can be commanded from a single station, is usually done on the plane table by the method of
explain: When a small area can be entirely observed and measured from one single station, the method of radiation is used to plot all the points directly from that station.

q: 11. The method of plane tabling commonly used for establishing the instrument stations only, is a
explain: Resection is specifically used to locate/establish the plane table's own instrument station with reference to already plotted points.

q: 12. Setting up the plane table consists of operations
explain: Basic setup involves getting the board horizontal (levelling) and placing the plotted point exactly over the ground station (centering).

q: 13. A disadvantage of plane table survey is
options: It is heavy, cumbersome and awkward to carry
It can't be used in wet climate
details may not be available while redrawing to a different scale
accessories are likely to be lost
explain: The large board and tripod make it physically more difficult to transport compared to a compass or a simple level.

q: 14. Placing the table over the station such that the station plotted on sheet is exactly above the corresponding station on the ground is
explain: Centering ensures the vertical axis of the plotted point and the ground station are aligned.

q: 15. The method of plane tabling generally adopted to obtain details and plotting inaccessible points is
explain: Intersection plots points by the crossing of rays from two different stations, which is ideal for points that cannot be reached to measure distance.

q: 16. The two point problem is
options: a case of resection method where no ray is required to be drawn from the proceeding station to the instrument station
locating the position of plane table by means of two visible well defined points
explain: It is a resection technique where the table is oriented and located using two known points, often involving an auxiliary station.

q: 17. The three point problem can be solved by
explain: Several methods exist to solve the three-point problem, including Lehmann's (trial and error) and Bessel's (graphical).

q: 18. The size of plane table is
explain: Standard surveying plane tables typically measure 600mm by 750mm.

q: 19. Three-point problem can be solved by
explain: The three-point problem for orienting a plane table can be solved by several standard techniques, including the tracing paper method, Bessel's (mechanical/graphical) method, and Lehmann's method, so all are valid solutions.

q: 20. Strength of fix of a plane table is
options: accuracy in locating the position of instrument station by taking observation to three stations
fixity of table while solving two point problem
explain: Strength of fix refers to how accurately the table's position is determined relative to the known points.

q: 21. The strength of fix' is poor when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the station is outside the great circle
the station is on the great circle
the station is within the great circle but outside the great triangle
explain: The position is indeterminate if the station is on the circumference of the great circle.

q: 22. To orient a plane table without two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted is
explain: The two-point problem is the specific procedure used to orient when only two points are available and distance measurement is not possible.

q: 23. The instrument used for centering the plane table accurately is
explain: The plumbing fork (or U-frame) carries a plumb bob to transfer the ground point to the paper.

q: 24. The orientation of the table is done by
explain: The table can be oriented using a compass (magnetic needle) or by aligning a line with a previously occupied station (back sighting).

q: 25. In case of telescopic alidade, the adjustment done is
options: the line of collimation should perpendicular to the axis of telescope
the horizontal axis should be parallel to the alidade rule
the bubble line of telescope level should be parallel to the plane of collimation
explain: Telescopic alidades require these permanent adjustments to ensure the line of sight accurately reflects the horizontal and vertical positions plotted on the sheet.

q: 26. Accuracy of 'fix' by two point problem, is
explain: Compared to the three-point problem, the accuracy of the 'fix' obtained by the two-point problem is generally not as reliable, since it involves an iterative trial-and-error graphical solution.

q: 27. While plane tabling in plane and open area, the most important operation for setting up the plane table is
explain: In plane and open terrain, leveling of the plane table is considered the most important initial operation for correctly setting up the instrument.

q: 28. The plane table surveying is
options: most suitable for preparing small-scale maps
less costly that a theodolite survey
explain: Plane table surveying offers multiple advantages together - it is suited for small-scale mapping, works well in areas with magnetic disturbance (since it doesn't rely on compass bearings), and is generally less costly than theodolite surveys - so all of the above apply.

q: 29. In plate tabling, the instrument used to measure horizontal and vertical distance directly is known as
explain: A telescopic alidade, fitted with stadia hairs, allows both horizontal and vertical distances to be measured directly during plane tabling without separate chaining.

q: 30. Which of the following methods of plane table surveying is used to locate the position of an inaccessible points?
explain: The intersection method in plane table surveying is used specifically to locate inaccessible points, by drawing rays from two known stations and marking their intersection.
